Professional Services

A professional services firm is bought on reputation, and the website is read before anyone calls: a prospect's procurement team checks it, and a referred contact looks for the partner's name on it. We build sites that pass that reading, that a marketing team publishes on without a developer, and that report monthly in a form a managing partner forwards unedited.

Where the Mandate Is Lost

Where a Firm's Website Loses the Mandate

The ProblemStandard Agency

Credentials sit where a reviewer cannot find them

A prospect's procurement team opens the site before the first call, looking for accreditations, insurance, data handling and who is accountable. Held in a PDF or a footer, none of it is found, and what a reviewer cannot find is marked as missing.

Partner pages give a referral nothing to confirm

Most professional services work arrives as a name passed on. The prospect searches that name and lands on a title and a headshot. With nothing about the matters handled, the sectors served or the writing published, the referral goes no further.

Each brand in the group fixes the same fault separately

A group with several brands or offices runs several sites, each with its own template and content library. A fix made on one never reaches the others, and when the board asks whether amends are being made across all the sites, nobody can answer per site.

The SolutionThe Legency Approach

Credentials placed where procurement looks

Accreditations, professional indemnity, data handling and the named people behind the work sit on a page that exists before anyone asks, placed where a reviewer goes first. The person sent to check finds what they were sent for, and the site says the firm can hold the engagement.

Partner pages that carry the referral to a call

Each partner and team page holds the matters handled, the sectors served, the writing published and a direct contact, built from components the marketing team fills in without a developer. A referred prospect confirms the name they were given and books the call from the page.

One system across every brand in the group

Builds, technical search work and AI visibility run across all sites as a single system with shared standards, so a fix lands on every brand at once. K2 Group's security team ran a 36-question due diligence questionnaire before that work began.

Built for the Firm

Four Things a Professional Services Engagement Delivers

Trust Signals a Reviewer Can Find

Accreditations, insurance, data handling and named accountability on pages a prospect's procurement team reaches in one click, so the legitimacy check passes before the first call.

Pages Your Team Publishes Without a Developer

Partner profiles, practice pages and insights built from locked components, so the marketing team adds a new partner or a new office the day it is announced and the page matches the rest of the site.

One System Across Brands and Languages

Shared standards on every site in the group, locale variants with translated URLs, and per-office publishing rights, so each market finds its own page and a change made once reaches every brand.

A Report the Board Reads Unedited

One report per site each month covering traffic, keywords, authority, AI visibility and work delivered, every number sourced, built to be forwarded to a managing partner or board without a briefing.

Trust on the Page

Procurement Reads the Site Before a Partner Calls

A professional services firm sells expertise and is bought on trust, so the website is read as evidence before the first conversation. Professional services website design starts from that reading: what a prospect's procurement team looks for, and what a referred contact needs to confirm.

Four pages, in the order a reviewer opens them.

  1. 01

    Credentials on a page that exists first

    Accreditations, regulatory registrations, professional indemnity and data handling belong on a page that exists before anyone asks, linked from the places a reviewer opens first. Buried in a PDF or held back for the proposal, they do not help the person sent to check.

  2. 02

    Partner pages that hold the sale

    The partner's name is what the referral passes on, so the partner's page holds the matters handled, the sectors served, the writing published and a direct route to a call. Built from components, it is updated by the marketing team the day a partner joins or is promoted.

  3. 03

    Insights that read as expertise

    Published thinking is the second thing a prospect reads. Every article on K2 Group's six sites was read against one test: would somebody type the title into a search engine without ever having heard of the firm.

    196
    posts passed the mechanical test
    53
    survived the editorial one
    205
    new answers, each grounded in its article
  4. 04

    A change record the board can ask for

    Who published which page, in which language, and when, is recorded per site. A regional office publishes its own market without touching the group hub, and the group has the answer ready when someone asks who changed what.

Answers That Name Firms

Buyers Ask an AI Assistant Which Firm to Shortlist

An HR director, a general counsel or a family office asks an assistant which firms handle a matter like theirs, and gets a shortlist. Coverage in those answers is measured per practice and per market, in the same monthly report as search.

Checked Every Month

Four engines, every practice, every market

  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Perplexity
  • Gemini

Each brand, practice and market is checked for the questions its buyers ask, in search rankings and in AI answers. The board sees which practices are covered, which are missing, and which brand should own each answer. A firm with one office gets the same read.

Content written for the question a buyer types

Answers are written for the question a buyer would type, each attached to the article it belongs to. That is how K2 Group's library grew from 244 to 449 answers.

The technical repair underneath

Assistants and search engines read the same site, so the repair counts twice. Across K2 Group's estate, 230 markup errors were closed and the group's brand search moved to first place.

Case Study

Five brands and a group hub run as one firm.

K2 Group is a global mobility group with relocation, immigration, advisory and communications brands on six Webflow sites. One partner took ownership of the whole group: 261 stranded URLs mapped off a retired domain, an FAQ library grown from 244 to 449 answers with 75 of them in French, Spanish, Portuguese and Mandarin, and a monthly per-site report built to go straight to the board.
